papers.title: Mechanics of Long-Context Hybrid Models Part 1.1: From Hybrid Attention to Hybrid Position
papers.problem: Teams mixing full attention with cheaper attention types lacked a clear reason why some mixes handle long text better.
papers.fix: A new sliding-window linear attention design reaches 16 times longer input without retraining and keeps 100% accuracy at 64k tokens.
papers.practicalUseCase: Pick the hybrid type for your job: linear hybrids gain more from long training, sliding-window hybrids stretch better untrained.
papers.limitation: It covers only two hybrid types, sliding-window and gated linear attention, and is only the first part of a series.

papers.title: Questioning the Questions: Sustaining Self-Evolution in Reasoning Models
papers.problem: Models that train on their own questions get worse each round because bad and repeated questions pile up.
papers.fix: R-Quest filters invalid questions and rewards new ones, and beat R-Zero by 17.32 points after ten rounds.
papers.practicalUseCase: Self-training can keep improving for ten rounds if you check question quality first, so filter bad questions before training.
papers.limitation: Tests covered math, general reasoning, and code on 12 benchmarks with two model families only.

papers.title: WebFovea: When the Model Is Right but the Click Is Wrong -- Reliable Round Trips for Vision-Based Web Agents on Live Websites
papers.problem: Web agents often fail on live sites because the code linking model and browser breaks, not the model.
papers.fix: Fixing that code, with the same model, raised the official score from 31.0 to 57.0 and won 2nd place.
papers.practicalUseCase: Before blaming the AI model, check your clicks and parsing; one bug put every click at three-quarters of its target.
papers.limitation: Scores come from live sites, so run-to-run variance can blur the gain, and some fixes depend on the model.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks set up sustainability committees, but nobody knew if they change environmental work in Islamic and conventional banks.
papers.fix: Committees link to higher scores in all four areas at conventional banks, but only two areas at Islamic banks.
papers.practicalUseCase: Islamic banks' committees may deliver symbolic results, so regulators should check for real green products, not just scores.
papers.limitation: Panel data shows links, not cause, and covers only emerging markets with both bank types.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Nobody had mapped how sustainability sukuk issuance grew or what makes an issue bigger.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 sukuk issues, equity-based contracts, strong security, and social purposes each go with larger sustainability sukuk issues.
papers.practicalUseCase: Issuers who want bigger sukuk can pick equity-based contracts, but costly second-party opinions shrink issue size.
papers.limitation: Sustainability sukuk stay a tiny share of the market, and the data stops at 2022.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan lacked proof that AI and big data help them compete and grow sustainably.
papers.fix: In a survey of 214 managers, AI, big data analytics, and data management all link to better competitiveness and sustainability.
papers.practicalUseCase: Staff digital skill helps a bank compete but not its sustainability results, so fund tools and data practices too.
papers.limitation: It is a one-time survey of Jordanian Islamic banks, so it shows links, not cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Leaders did not know which of ICT, high-tech exports, or institutions drives bank growth in dual banking systems.
papers.fix: Across 218 banks in 12 countries, ICT adoption drives growth most, and high-tech exports help only alongside ICT.
papers.practicalUseCase: Going digital helps both bank types grow, and strong governance supports Islamic banks especially.
papers.limitation: Data covers only 12 countries from 2010 to 2023, so results may not hold elsewhere.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Muslim-majority countries still exclude many people from banking, despite Islamic finance growing fast, and the causes were unclear.
papers.fix: In 35 countries from 2005 to 2021, income, tertiary education, institutions, and internet access shape inclusion in OIC states.
papers.practicalUseCase: Governments in OIC states should invest in digital infrastructure, youth and women, and income growth, unlike OECD peers.
papers.limitation: The estimates cover only 35 OIC and OECD countries, so single-country results may differ.

papers.title: Psychometric properties of the Arabic Perceived Digital Well-Being Scale (PDWS) in Saudi young adults
papers.institution: Imam Mohammad ibn Saud Islamic University
papers.problem: Research on young people's phones focused on risks, leaving no balanced tool to measure digital well-being in Arabic.
papers.fix: The Arabic scale shows three clear domains, and ties to higher life satisfaction and lower fear of missing out.
papers.practicalUseCase: Teams can now track phone well-being, not just addiction, among Arabic-speaking young adults.
papers.limitation: Online volunteers from Riyadh aged 18 to 25 took a one-time survey, so results show links, not cause.
